question: how long would you expect it to load a new section, give me an estimate
answer:
Rough estimate, split by phase, for your 1.2-sized section (12 pages, 30 topics, 3 crops):

| Phase | Before | Now (expected) |
|---|---|---|
| Author: reads/views/crops/inventory | ~25 serial turns | 4–5 turns (batched 4 per message) |
| Author: writing the lesson | 15–40 turns at your `max` thinking level | unchanged — still the dominant cost |
| Review crew | 38 packets, 6 workers, 26 checks in 8.6 min before you cancelled | 17 packets, 12 workers → 2 waves, ~40 s – 2 min |
| Question reviews | 2–3 requests each | 1 request each, ~10–20 s |

Realistic total: **~5–10 minutes** for a dense new section, worst case ~15 min if your provider is slow that day — down from the 20–30 min you saw. The crew is no longer the bottleneck; your authoring model running at `max` thinking is.

Two caveats worth knowing:
- The first `lessonComplete` after this update re-runs the whole crew once (the packet cache key changed); later edits re-run only the affected packets (seconds).
- The estimate assumes `deepseek-flash`-class latency for reviewers, which is now pinned to `low` reasoning regardless of your session level, so it won't creep back up when you switch the session to `max`.

Cheap levers if a section still feels slow: the crew fallbacks in order — concurrency 12→16, teaching groups 4→8 topics per packet, source windows 4→8 pages. Author-side, the real win is dropping section-level thinking from `max` to `high`/`medium`, which nothing in this change forced.
